title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: S is smooth, irreducible and of finite type over Q, with function field K. U = U_S → S is an 'elementary' relative scheme in the sense of SGA 4 XI (Artin's 'bons voisinages'). It is built from successive relative curves whose fibres are anabelian (hyperbolic), or at least have non-trivial π1. 'Diagram 5' (an earlier page) is the commutative diagram of profinite groups built from:
- E_K = Gal(K̄/K) and E_S = π1(S);
- E_{U_K} = π1(U_K) and E_{U_S} = π1(U);
- the surjections E_K → E_S and E_{U_K} → E_{U_S};
- the extensions E_{U_K} → E_K and E_{U_S} → E_S, which have geometric kernel π1 of the geometric generic fibre.

A rational section f of U → S is a K-point of U_K. It defines a section s_f : E_K → E_{U_K}, well defined up to conjugation by the geometric kernel. Composing with E_{U_K} → E_{U_S} gives a homomorphism E_K → E_{U_S} lifting the surjection E_K → E_S.

The statement Grothendieck sets out to prove: f is everywhere defined (f extends to a section S → U) iff s_f descends to a section E_S → E_{U_S}. Equivalently, the lift E_K → E_{U_S} kills (s'annule sur) the kernel of E_K → E_S. That kernel is the closed normal subgroup generated by the inertia groups at all points of S, in effect at the codimension-1 points.

The direction 'f extends ⇒ the section descends' is formal: the section is then induced by π1 of the morphism S → U. The converse is a relative or integral analogue of the section conjecture, a 'Néron-type' extension criterion read off from the fundamental group.

The next page begins the proof strategy:
- The condition is of codimension 1. By Zariski–Nagata purity, π1(S∖Y) ≅ π1(S) for Y of codimension ≥ 2.
- Since a rational map from a normal S to U (affine over S) extends across codimension ≥ 2 once it is defined in codimension 1, one is reduced to DVRs at the generic points of divisors.
- There one expects to argue as follows. If the K-point meets a boundary divisor (a cusp) of the relative compactification with multiplicity m > 0, the inertia of the DVR maps non-trivially into the cuspidal inertia, so the section is 'ramified'. Conversely, unramified means the point specializes into U.

The broader purpose, stated on the previous page, is to describe smooth schemes over finitely generated fields, and their étale topoi, through extensions of profinite groups. This page tests that the group-theoretic description correctly encodes which rational sections are regular.
errors: No mathematical error on the page. The non-trivial direction is only announced, not proved here.

Gap: as stated, it should rely on fibres being hyperbolic/anabelian (or at least the boundary inertia injecting into π1). For fibres with π1 = 0 or abelian non-hyperbolic cases (e.g. G_m fibres) the criterion still works via Kummer theory, but for fibres like A^1 it fails. Grothendieck's hedge 'à π1 non nul' hints he saw this condition.

The equivalence 'section of E_{U_K} over E_K comes from a section of E_{U_S} over E_S' ⇔ 'the lift kills ker(E_K → E_S)' presupposes that E_{U_K} → E_K is the pullback of E_{U_S} → E_S. This holds for elementary fibrations, by the homotopy exact sequence and generic-fibre comparison.

ideas.what: Group-theoretic criterion for a rational section of an elementary (anabelian) fibration over a smooth Q-base to be regular: the associated Galois section must be unramified, i.e. descend from Gal(K) to π1(S).
ideas.modern_name: integral/relative (unramified) section conjecture; extension of rational points via unramified sections
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in Grothendieck's 1983 letter to Faltings. Developed for curves over DVRs and number rings by Nakamura, Tamagawa, Mochizuki, Stix (e.g. Stix's 'Rational points and arithmetic of fundamental groups', 2013)
ideas.where_published: Section conjecture in the letter to Faltings (1983). This relative extension criterion is not, to my knowledge, in his published texts.

ideas.what: Reduction of the extension problem to codimension 1 via Zariski–Nagata purity of the branch locus (π1(S∖Y) = π1(S) for codim Y ≥ 2).
ideas.usually_credited_to: Zariski, Nagata; Grothendieck SGA 1 X, SGA 2
ideas.where_published: SGA 1 Exp. X §3; SGA 2 Exp. X

ideas.what: Use of elementary fibrations (Artin neighbourhoods) as the building blocks for anabelian descriptions of smooth schemes over finitely generated fields.
ideas.modern_name: Artin elementary fibrations / good neighbourhoods; anabelian geometry of higher-dimensional varieties
ideas.usually_credited_to: M. Artin (SGA 4 XI); anabelian use by Grothendieck, later Mochizuki, Schmidt–Stix
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme; letter to Faltings (as a programme)

missed.claim: A precise higher-dimensional 'unramified section ⇔ regular section' criterion for elementary anabelian fibrations over a smooth base over Q, with an explicit purity-plus-local-cusp-inertia strategy. Grothendieck frames it as a step toward reconstructing smooth schemes and their étale topoi from profinite extensions.
missed.quote: Je veux montrer que f est partout définie, i.e. une section de U_S sur S, ssi la section de E_{U_K} sur E_K provient d'une section de E_{U_S} sur E_S
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Relative/integral versions of the section conjecture over higher-dimensional bases are studied but scattered. This is an early explicit formulation by Grothendieck, apparently c. 1981, predating the Faltings letter. It is of historical interest, though the curve-over-DVR case is by now fairly standard.

deep.surprise_reason: An early, explicit formulation of the relative (unramified) section-extension criterion over a higher-dimensional base, with a purity reduction. Historically interesting as anticipating later integral section-conjecture work, but the mathematics is close to what specialists know, and the page contains only the statement.
transcription_corrections: 'ou des moins' should read 'ou du moins'.
'S étant lui — (pour fixer les idées)' should read 'S étant lui-même (pour fixer les idées)'.
Last line: 'se factorise par[?]' is more likely 's'annule sur' (continuing 'le noyau de E_K → E_S' on the next page); this fits the mathematics.
The insertion above 'relèvement' is uncertain ('sortant[?]'). It may read 'de section' or similar; the parenthetical reads '(composé de E_K → E_{U_K} avec E_{U_K} → E_{U_S})'.
